sanskrit:
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच
धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः।
मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय
translation:
Dhritarashtra said, "What did my people
and the sons of Pandu do when they had
assembled together, eager for battle, on
the holy plain of Kurukshetra, O Sanjaya?"
explanation:
Dharmakshetra -- that place which protects
Dharma is Dharmakshetra. Because it was in
the land of the Kurus? it was called
Kurukshetra.Sanjaya is one who has conered

sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच
दृष्ट्वा तु पाण्डवानीकं व्यूढं दुर्योधनस्तदा।
आचार्यमुपसङ्गम्य राजा वचनमब्रवीत्
translation:
Sanjaya said: Having seen the army of the
Pandavas drawn up in battle array, King
Duryodhana approached his teacher, Drona,
and spoke these words.
explanation:
Sanjaya replied: "When Prince Duryodhana
saw the Pandavas' army paraded, he
approached his preceptor Guru Drona and
spoke these words:

sanskrit:
पश्यैतां पाण्डुपुत्राणामाचार्य महतीं चमूम्।
व्यूढां द्रुपदपुत्रेण तव शिष्येण धीमता
translation:
Behold, O Teacher! This mighty army of the
sons of Pandu, arrayed by the son of
Drupada, thy wise disciple.
explanation:
Revered Father! Behold this mighty host of
the Pandavas, paraded by the son of King
Drupada, your wise disciple.

sanskrit:
अत्र शूरा महेष्वासा भीमार्जुनसमा युधि।
युयुधानो विराटश्च द्रुपदश्च महारथः
translation:
Here are heroes, mighty archers, equal in
battle to Bhima and Arjuna, Yuyudhana
(Satyaki), Virata, and Drupada—all mighty
warriors.
explanation:
Technically? maharatha means a warrior who
is proficient in the science of war and
who is able to fight alone with ten
thousand archers.

sanskrit:
धृष्टकेतुश्चेकितानः काशिराजश्च वीर्यवान्।
पुरुजित्कुन्तिभोजश्च शैब्यश्च नरपुङ्गवः
translation:
Dhrishtaketu, Chekitana, the valiant king
of Kasi, Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and
Saibya—the best of men.
explanation:
Dhrishtaketu, Chekitan, the valiant king
of Benares, Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and
Shaibya—a master of many.

sanskrit:
युधामन्युश्च विक्रान्त उत्तमौजाश्च वीर्यवान्।
सौभद्रो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्व एव महारथाः
translation:
The strong Yudhamanyu and the brave
Uttamaujas, the son of Subhadra
(Abhimanyu, the son of Subhadra and
Arjuna), and the sons of Draupadi, all of
explanation:
Yudhamanyu, Uttamouja, Soubhadra, and the
sons of Droupadi—all famous men.

sanskrit:
अस्माकं तु विशिष्टा ये तान्निबोध द्विजोत्तम।
नायका मम सैन्यस्य संज्ञार्थं तान्ब्रवीमि ते
translation:
Know also, O best among the twice-born!
the names of those who are the most
distinguished amongst ourselves, the
leaders of my army; these I name to you
explanation: No changes needed.

sanskrit:
भवान्भीष्मश्च कर्णश्च कृपश्च समितिञ्जयः।
अश्वत्थामा विकर्णश्च सौमदत्तिस्तथैव च
translation:
"Thou thyself, Bhishma, Karna, Kripa, the
victorious in war, Asvatthama, Vikarna,
and Bhurisrava, the son of Somadatta—all
these are ready for battle."

sanskrit:
अन्ये च बहवः शूरा मदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः।
नानाशस्त्रप्रहरणाः सर्वे युद्धविशारदाः
translation:
And also many other heroes, ready to give
up their lives for my sake, armed with
various weapons and missiles, all
well-skilled in battle.
explanation:
And many others, all ready to die for My
sake; all armed, all skilled in warfare.

sanskrit:
अपर्याप्तं तदस्माकं बलं भीष्माभिरक्षितम्।
पर्याप्तं त्विदमेतेषां बलं भीमाभिरक्षितम्
translation:
Our army, marshalled by Bhishma, is
insufficient, whereas theirs, marshalled
by Bhima, is sufficient.
explanation:
The verse is differently interpreted by
different commentators. Sridhara Swami
takes the word aparyaptam to mean
insufficient.

sanskrit:
अयनेषु च सर्वेषु यथाभागमवस्थिताः।
भीष्ममेवाभिरक्षन्तु भवन्तः सर्व एव हि
translation:
Therefore, do all of you, stationed in
your respective positions in the several
divisions of the army, protect Bhishma
alone.
explanation:
Therefore, let the rank and file stand
firm in their posts according to
battalions, and all you generals around
Bheeshma.

sanskrit:
तस्य संजनयन्हर्षं कुरुवृद्धः पितामहः।
सिंहनादं विनद्योच्चैः शङ्खं दध्मौ प्रतापवान्
translation:
His glorious grandsire, the oldest of the
Kauravas, roared like a lion to cheer
Duryodhana and blew his conch.
explanation:
Then, to enliven his spirits, the brave
Grandfather Bheeshma, the eldest of the
Kuru clan, blew his conch, its sound
resembling that of a lion's roar.

sanskrit:
ततः शङ्खाश्च भेर्यश्च पणवानकगोमुखाः।
सहसैवाभ्यहन्यन्त स शब्दस्तुमुलोऽभवत्
translation:
Then, suddenly, conches, kettledrums,
tabors, drums, and cow horns blared forth
from the Kaurava side, and the sound was
tremendous.
explanation:
And immediately, all the conches, drums,
trumpets, and horns blared forth in a
tumultuous uproar.

sanskrit:
ततः श्वेतैर्हयैर्युक्ते महति स्यन्दने स्थितौ।
माधवः पाण्डवश्चैव दिव्यौ शङ्खौ प्रदध्मतुः
translation:
Then, Madhava (Krishna) and the son of
Pandu (Arjuna), seated in the magnificent
chariot yoked with white horses, blew
divine conches.
explanation:
Then, seated in their spacious war
chariot, yoked with white horses, Lord
Shri Krishna and Arjuna sounded their
divine conch shells.

sanskrit:
पाञ्चजन्यं हृषीकेशो देवदत्तं धनंजयः।
पौण्ड्रं दध्मौ महाशङ्खं भीमकर्मा वृकोदरः
translation:
Hrishikesha blew the Panchajanya, Arjuna
blew the Devadatta, and Bhima, the
wolf-bellied doer of terrible deeds, blew
the great conch Paundra.
explanation:
Lord Shri Krishna blew his Panchajanya,
and Arjuna blew his Devadatta; brave
Bheema blew his renowned shell, Poundra.

sanskrit:
अनन्तविजयं राजा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः।
नकुलः सहदेवश्च सुघोषमणिपुष्पकौ
translation:
King Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, blew
the Anantavijaya; Nakula and Sahadeva blew
the Sughosha and the Manipushpaka.
explanation:
The King Dharmaraja, the son of Kunti,
blew the Anantavijaya, Nakula, and
Sahadeva, the Sughosa and Manipushpaka,
respectively.

sanskrit:
काश्यश्च परमेष्वासः शिखण्डी च महारथः।
धृष्टद्युम्नो विराटश्च सात्यकिश्चापराजितः
translation:
The king of Kasi, an excellent archer,
Sikhandi, the mighty car-warrior,
Dhrishtadyumna, Virata, and Satyaki, the
unconquered.
explanation:
And the Maharaja of Benares, the great
archer, Shikhandi, the great soldier,
Dhrishtayumna, Virata, and Satyaki, the
invincible one,

sanskrit:
द्रुपदो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्वशः पृथिवीपते।
सौभद्रश्च महाबाहुः शङ्खान्दध्मुः पृथक्पृथक्
translation:
Drupada and the sons of Draupadi, O Lord
of the Earth, and the son of Subhadra, the
mighty-armed, blew their conches each
separately.
explanation:
This blowing of conches announced the
commencement of the battle.

sanskrit:
स घोषो धार्तराष्ट्राणां हृदयानि व्यदारयत्।
नभश्च पृथिवीं चैव तुमुलो व्यनुनादयन्
translation:
The tumultuous sound rent the hearts of
Dhritarashtra's party, reverberating
through both heaven and earth.
explanation:
The tumult rent the hearts of the sons of
Dhritarashtra, shaking heaven and earth
with its echoing violence.

sanskrit:
अथ व्यवस्थितान् दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रान्कपिध्वजः।
प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसंपाते धनुरुद्यम्य पाण्डवः
translation:
Then, seeing the people of Dhritarashtra's
party standing arrayed and the discharge
of weapons about to begin, Arjuna, the son
of Pandu whose ensign was a monkey, took
explanation:
Then, upon beholding the sons of
Dhritarashtra, drawn up on the
battlefield, ready to fight, Arjuna, whose
flag bore the image of Hanuman,

sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच
हृषीकेशं तदा वाक्यमिदमाह महीपते।
सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये रथं स्थापय मेऽच्युत
translation:
Arjuna said, "O Krishna, place my chariot
in the middle between the two armies, so
that I may behold those who stand here,
desirous to fight, and know with whom I
explanation:
Raising his bow, he spoke this to the Lord
Shri Krishna: O Infallible Lord of the
earth! Please draw up my chariot between
the two armies.

sanskrit:
यावदेतान्निरीक्षेऽहं योद्धुकामानवस्थितान्।
कैर्मया सह योद्धव्यमस्मिन्रणसमुद्यमे
translation:
Arjuna said, "O Krishna, place my chariot
in the middle between the two armies, so
that I may behold those who stand here,
desirous to fight, and know with whom I
explanation:
So that I may observe those who must fight
on my side and those who must fight
against me.

sanskrit:
योत्स्यमानानवेक्षेऽहं य एतेऽत्र समागताः।
धार्तराष्ट्रस्य दुर्बुद्धेर्युद्धे प्रियचिकीर्षवः
translation:
For I desire to observe those who are
assembled here to fight, wishing to please
in battle the evil-minded Duryodhana—the
son of Dhritarashtra.
explanation:
And gaze upon this array of soldiers,
eager to please the sons of Dhritarashtra
who are sinful.

sanskrit:
संजय उवाच
एवमुक्तो हृषीकेशो गुडाकेशेन भारत।
सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये स्थापयित्वा रथोत्तमम्
translation:
Sanjaya said, Thus addressed by Arjuna,
Krishna stationed the best of chariots, O
Dhritarashtra, in the midst of the two
armies.
explanation:
Sanjaya said: "Having listened to Arjuna's
request, Lord Shri Krishna drew up His
bright chariot in the midst between the
two armies.

sanskrit:
भीष्मद्रोणप्रमुखतः सर्वेषां च महीक्षिताम्।
उवाच पार्थ पश्यैतान्समवेतान्कुरूनिति
translation:
In front of Bhishma and Drona, and all the
rulers of the earth, he said: "O Arjuna,
son of Pritha, behold these Kurus gathered
together."
explanation:
Where Bheeshma and Drona had led all the
rulers of the earth, they spoke thus: O
Arjuna! Behold, these members of the
family of Kuru are assembled.

sanskrit:
तत्रापश्यत्स्थितान्पार्थः पितृ़नथ पितामहान्।
आचार्यान्मातुलान्भ्रातृ़न्पुत्रान्पौत्रान्सखींस्तथा
translation:
Then, Arjuna (son of Pritha) saw there (in
the armies) stationed fathers,
grandfathers, teachers, maternal uncles,
brothers, sons, grandsons, and friends.
explanation:
There, Arjuna noticed fathers,
grandfathers, uncles, cousins, sons,
grandsons, teachers, and friends.

sanskrit:
श्वशुरान्सुहृदश्चैव सेनयोरुभयोरपि।
तान्समीक्ष्य स कौन्तेयः सर्वान्बन्धूनवस्थितान्
translation:
He saw fathers-in-law and friends in both
the armies. The son of Kunti, Arjuna,
seeing all those kinsmen thus standing
arrayed, spoke sorrowfully, deeply filled
explanation:
Fathers-in-law and benefactors were
arrayed on both sides, and Arjuna then
gazed at all those kinsmen before him.

sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच
कृपया परयाऽऽविष्टो विषीदन्निदमब्रवीत्।
दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम्
translation:
Arjuna said, "O Krishna, seeing my kinsmen
arrayed here, eager to fight,
explanation:
And his heart melted with pity, and sadly
he spoke: "O my Lord! When I see all
these, my own people, thirsting for
battle,

sanskrit:
सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति।
वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते
translation:
My limbs fail, my mouth is parched, my
body quivers, and my hair stands on end.
explanation:
My limbs are failing me, my throat is
parched, my body is trembling, and my hair
is standing on end.

sanskrit:
गाण्डीवं स्रंसते हस्तात्त्वक्चैव परिदह्यते।
न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः
translation:
The Gandiva slips from my hand, and my
skin burns all over; I am unable to stand,
and my mind is reeling, as it were.
explanation:
The bow Gandiva slips from my hand, and my
skin burns. I cannot remain still, for my
mind is in tumult.

sanskrit:
निमित्तानि च पश्यामि विपरीतानि केशव।
न च श्रेयोऽनुपश्यामि हत्वा स्वजनमाहवे
translation:
And I see ill omens, O Kesava. I do not
see any good in slaying my kinsmen in
battle.
explanation:
Kesava means he who has fine or luxuriant
hair.

sanskrit:
न काङ्क्षे विजयं कृष्ण न च राज्यं सुखानि च।
किं नो राज्येन गोविन्द किं भोगैर्जीवितेन वा
translation:
I desire not victory, O Krishna, nor
kingdom, nor pleasures. What use is
dominion to us, O Krishna, or pleasures or
even life?
explanation:
Ah, my Lord! I do not crave victory, nor a
kingdom, nor any pleasure. What would a
kingdom, happiness, or life be to me?

sanskrit:
येषामर्थे काङ्क्षितं नो राज्यं भोगाः सुखानि च।
त इमेऽवस्थिता युद्धे प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा धनानि च
translation:
Those for whose sake we desire kingdom,
enjoyments, and pleasures stand here in
battle, having renounced life and wealth.
explanation:
When those for whose sake I desire these
things stand here, about to sacrifice
their property and lives:

sanskrit:
आचार्याः पितरः पुत्रास्तथैव च पितामहाः।
मातुलाः श्चशुराः पौत्राः श्यालाः सम्बन्धिनस्तथा
translation:
Teachers, fathers, sons, and grandfathers,
maternal uncles, fathers-in-law,
grandsons, brothers-in-law, and other
relatives—
explanation:
Teachers, fathers, grandfathers, sons,
grandsons, uncles, fathers-in-law,
brothers-in-law, and other relatives.

sanskrit:
एतान्न हन्तुमिच्छामि घ्नतोऽपि मधुसूदन।
अपि त्रैलोक्यराज्यस्य हेतोः किं नु महीकृते
translation:
These I do not wish to kill, O Krishna,
even though they kill me, for the sake of
dominion over the three worlds; leave
alone killing them for the sake of the
explanation:
I would not kill them, even for three
worlds; why then for this earth alone? It
matters not if I myself am killed.

sanskrit:
निहत्य धार्तराष्ट्रान्नः का प्रीतिः स्याज्जनार्दन।
पापमेवाश्रयेदस्मान्हत्वैतानाततायिनः
translation:
By killing these sons of Dhritarashtra,
what pleasure could be ours, O Janardana?
Only sin would accrue to us from killing
these felons.
explanation:
Duryodhana had done all these evil
actions.

sanskrit:
तस्मान्नार्हा वयं हन्तुं धार्तराष्ट्रान्स्वबान्धवान्।
स्वजनं हि कथं हत्वा सुखिनः स्याम माधव
translation:
Therefore, we should not kill the sons of
Dhritarashtra, our relatives; for how can
we be happy by killing our own kin, O
Madhava (Krishna)?
explanation:
We are worthy of a nobler feat than
slaughtering our relatives—the sons of
Dhritarashtra; for, my Lord, how can we be
happy if we kill our kinsmen?

sanskrit:
यद्यप्येते न पश्यन्ति लोभोपहतचेतसः।
कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं मित्रद्रोहे च पातकम्
translation:
Though they, with intelligence overpowered
by greed, see no evil in the destruction
of families and no sin in hostility to
friends,
explanation:
Although these men, blinded by greed, see
no guilt in destroying their kin or
fighting against their friends,

sanskrit:
कथं न ज्ञेयमस्माभिः पापादस्मान्निवर्तितुम्।
कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं प्रपश्यद्भिर्जनार्दन
translation:
Why should we not, who clearly see the
evil in the destruction of families, learn
to turn away from this sin, O Janardana
(Krishna)?
explanation:
Ignorance of law is no excuse but wanton
sinful conduct is a grave crime? unworthy
of us? who are wiser.

sanskrit:
कुलक्षये प्रणश्यन्ति कुलधर्माः सनातनाः।
धर्मे नष्टे कुलं कृत्स्नमधर्मोऽभिभवत्युत
translation:
In the destruction of a family, the
immemorial religious rites of that family
perish; on the destruction of
spirituality, impiety indeed, overwhelms
explanation:
Dharma -- the duties and ceremonies
practised by the family in accordance with
the injunctions of the scriptures.

sanskrit:
अधर्माभिभवात्कृष्ण प्रदुष्यन्ति कुलस्त्रियः।
स्त्रीषु दुष्टासु वार्ष्णेय जायते वर्णसङ्करः
translation:
O Krishna, by the prevalence of impiety,
the women of the family become corrupt;
and, when women are corrupted, O Varshenya
(descendant of Vrishni), intermingling of
explanation:
When irreligion spreads, the women of the
house start to stray; when they lose their
purity, adulteration of the lineage
follows.

sanskrit:
सङ्करो नरकायैव कुलघ्नानां कुलस्य च।
पतन्ति पितरो ह्येषां लुप्तपिण्डोदकक्रियाः
translation:
Confusion of castes leads to hell for the
slayers of the family, for their forebears
fall, deprived of the offerings of
rice-balls and libations of water.
explanation:
Promiscuity ruins both the family and
those who defile it; while the souls of
our ancestors droop, due to the lack of
funeral cakes and ablutions.

sanskrit:
दोषैरेतैः कुलघ्नानां वर्णसङ्करकारकैः।
उत्साद्यन्ते जातिधर्माः कुलधर्माश्च शाश्वताः
translation:
By these evil deeds of the destroyers of
the family, which cause confusion of
castes, the eternal religious rites of the
caste and the family are destroyed.
explanation:
By the destruction of our lineage and the
pollution of our blood, ancient class
traditions and family purity alike perish.

sanskrit:
उत्सन्नकुलधर्माणां मनुष्याणां जनार्दन।
नरकेऽनियतं वासो भवतीत्यनुशुश्रुम
translation:
We have heard, O Janardana, that those men
in whose families the religious practices
have been destroyed are inevitably
destined to dwell in hell for an unknown
explanation:
The wise say, my Lord, that they are
forever lost whose ancient traditions have
been lost.

sanskrit:
अहो बत महत्पापं कर्तुं व्यवसिता वयम्।
यद्राज्यसुखलोभेन हन्तुं स्वजनमुद्यताः
translation:
Alas! We are involved in a great sin, for
we are prepared to kill our kinsmen, out
of greed for the pleasures of a kingdom.
explanation:
Alas, it is strange that we should be
willing to kill our own countrymen and
commit a great sin, in order to enjoy the
pleasures of kingdom.

sanskrit:
यदि मामप्रतीकारमशस्त्रं शस्त्रपाणयः।
धार्तराष्ट्रा रणे हन्युस्तन्मे क्षेमतरं भवेत्
translation:
If the sons of Dhritarashtra, with weapons
in hand, should slay me in battle,
unresisting and unarmed, that would be
better for me.
explanation:
If, on the contrary, the sons of
Dhritarashtra, with weapons in hand,
should slay me, unarmed and unresisting,

sanskrit:

विसृज्य सशरं चापं शोकसंविग्नमानसः
translation:
Sanjaya said, Having thus spoken in the

explanation:
Sanjaya said: "Having spoken thus, Arjuna
sank into the seat of his chariot,
discarding his bow and arrow, overwhelmed
with grief in the midst of the armies."

विषीदन्तमिदं वाक्यमुवाच मधुसूदनः

Sanjaya said: To him, who was thus

Sanjaya then told how the Lord Shri
Krishna, seeing Arjuna overwhelmed with
compassion, his eyes dimmed with flowing
tears and full of despondency, consoled

sanskrit:

कुतस्त्वा कश्मलमिदं विषमे समुपस्थितम्।
अनार्यजुष्टमस्वर्ग्यमकीर्तिकरमर्जुन
translation:
The Blessed Lord said, "From whence has
this perilous strait come upon you, this
dejection which is unworthy of you,

explanation:
The Lord said: My beloved friend! Why
yield to this weakness, on the eve of
battle, which does no credit to those who

sanskrit:
क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते।
क्षुद्रं हृदयदौर्बल्यं त्यक्त्वोत्तिष्ठ परन्तप
translation:
Do not yield to impotence, O Arjuna, son
of Pritha. It does not befit you. Cast off
this mean weakness of the heart! Stand up,
O conqueror of foes!
explanation:
O Arjuna! Why give way to unmanliness? O
thou, who art the terror of thy enemies!
Shake off such shameful effeminacy and
make ready to act!

sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच
कथं भीष्ममहं संख्ये द्रोणं च मधुसूदन।
इषुभिः प्रतियोत्स्यामि पूजार्हावरिसूदन
translation:
Arjuna said, "O Madhusudana, how can I
fight in battle with arrows against
Bhishma and Drona, who are worthy of being
worshipped, O destroyer of enemies?"
explanation:
Arjuna argued: My Lord! How can I, when
the battle rages, send an arrow through
Bheeshma and Drona, whom I should revere?

sanskrit:
गुरूनहत्वा हि महानुभावान्
श्रेयो भोक्तुं भैक्ष्यमपीह लोके।
हत्वार्थकामांस्तु गुरूनिहैव
भुञ्जीय भोगान् रुधिरप्रदिग्धान्
translation:
Better it is, indeed, in this world to
accept alms than to slay the most noble
teachers. But if I were to kill them, even
in this world, all my enjoyments of wealth
explanation:
Rather, I would be content with a beggar's
crust than to kill these teachers of mine,
these precious noble souls! To slay these
masters who are my benefactors would be to

sanskrit:

यद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः।
यानेव हत्वा न जिजीविषाम
स्तेऽवस्थिताः प्रमुखे धार्तराष्ट्राः
translation:
I can hardly tell which would be better,
that we should conquer them or that they
should conquer us. Even the sons of
Dhritarashtra, whom we do not wish to
explanation:
Nor can I say whether it would be better
for them to conquer me or for me to
conquer them, since I would no longer care
to live if I killed these sons of

sanskrit:
कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावः
पृच्छामि त्वां धर्मसंमूढचेताः।
यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्िचतं ब्रूहि तन्मे
शिष्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम्
translation:
My heart is overpowered by the taint of
pity; my mind is confused as to my duty. I
ask Thee: Tell me decisively what is good
for me. I am Thy disciple; instruct me,
explanation:
My heart is oppressed with pity, and my
mind is confused as to what my duty is.
Therefore, my Lord, tell me what is best
for my spiritual welfare, for I am Your

sanskrit:
न हि प्रपश्यामि ममापनुद्या
द्यच्छोकमुच्छोषणमिन्द्रियाणाम्।
अवाप्य भूमावसपत्नमृद्धम्
राज्यं सुराणामपि चाधिपत्यम्
translation:
I do not see that this sorrow that burns
up my senses would be removed, even if I
were to attain prosperous and unrivaled
dominion on earth or lordship over the
explanation:
For even if I were to attain the monarchy
of the visible world, or the sovereignty
over the invisible world, it would not
drive away the anguish that is now

sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच
एवमुक्त्वा हृषीकेशं गुडाकेशः परन्तप।
न योत्स्य इति गोविन्दमुक्त्वा तूष्णीं बभूव ह
translation:
Sanjaya said: Having spoken thus to
Hrishikesha, the Lord of the senses,
Arjuna, the conqueror of sleep and
destroyer of foes, said, "I will not
explanation:
Sanjaya continued: "Arjuna, the conqueror
of all enemies, then told the Lord of
All-Hearts that he would not fight, and
became silent, O King!

sanskrit:
तमुवाच हृषीकेशः प्रहसन्निव भारत।
सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये विषीदन्तमिदं वचः
translation:
To him who was despondent in the midst of
the two armies, Krishna, smiling, O
Bharata, spoke these words.
explanation:
Thereupon, the Lord, with a gracious
smile, addressed him who was so much
depressed in the midst of the two armies.

sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच
अशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे।
गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः
translation:
The Blessed Lord said, "You have grieved
for those who should not be grieved for;
yet, you speak words of wisdom. The wise
grieve neither for the living nor for the
explanation:
-- The philosophy of the Gita begins from
this verse.Bhishma and Drona deserve no
grief because they are eternal in their
real nature and they are virtuous men who

sanskrit:
न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः।
न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयमतः परम्
translation:
Nor, at any time, was I not, nor thou, nor
these rulers of men; nor, verily, shall we
ever cease to be hereafter.
explanation:
-- Lord Krishna speaks here of the
immortality of the Soul or the
imperishable nature of the Self (Atman).
The Soul exists in the three periods of

sanskrit:
देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा।
तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति
translation:
Just as the embodied soul passes through
childhood, youth, and old age in this
body, so too does it pass into another
body; the steadfast one does not grieve
explanation:
-- Just as there is no interruption in the
passing of childhood into youth and youth
into old age in this body? so also there
is no interruption by death in the

sanskrit:
मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः।
आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत
translation:
The contact of the senses with the
objects, O son of Kunti, which causes heat
and cold, pleasure and pain, has a
beginning and an end; they are
explanation:
-- Cold is pleasant at one time and
painful at another. Heat is pleasant in
winter but painful in summer.

sanskrit:
यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ।
समदुःखसुखं धीरं सोऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते
translation:
That firm man, whom surely these
afflictions do not, O chief among men, to
whom pleasure and pain are the same, is
fit for attaining immortality.
explanation:
-- Dehadhyasa or identification of the
Self with the body is the cause of
pleasure and pain. Calm endurance in
pleasure and pain? and heat and cold is

sanskrit:
नासतो विद्यते भावो नाभावो विद्यते सतः।
उभयोरपि दृष्टोऽन्तस्त्वनयोस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः
translation:
The unreal has no being; there is no
non-being of the real; the truth about
both has been seen by the knowers of the
truth (or the seers of the essence).
explanation:
-- The changeless? homogeneous Atman or
the Self always exists. It is the only
solid Reality.

sanskrit:
अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन सर्वमिदं ततम्।
विनाशमव्ययस्यास्य न कश्चित् कर्तुमर्हति
translation:
Know that to be indestructible, by which
all this is pervaded. No one can cause the
destruction of that, the Imperishable.
explanation:
The Spirit, which pervades all that is
seen, is imperishable. Nothing can destroy
it.

sanskrit:
अन्तवन्त इमे देहा नित्यस्योक्ताः शरीरिणः।
अनाशिनोऽप्रमेयस्य तस्माद्युध्यस्व भारत
translation:
These bodies of the embodied Self, which
are eternal, indestructible, and
immeasurable, are said to have an end.
Therefore, fight, O Arjuna.
explanation:
-- Lord Krishna explains to Arjuna the
nature of the allpervading? immortal Self
in a variety of ways and thus induces him
to fight by removing his delusion? grief

sanskrit:
य एनं वेत्ति हन्तारं यश्चैनं मन्यते हतम्।
उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायं हन्ति न हन्यते
translation:
He who takes the Self to be the slayer and
he who thinks it is slain, neither of them
knows. It does not slay, nor is it slain.
explanation:
-- The Self is nondoer (Akarta) and as It
is immutable? It is neither the agent nor
the object of the act of slaying. He who
thinks I slay or I am slain with the body

sanskrit:
न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचि
न्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः।
अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो
न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे
translation:
It is not born, nor does it ever die;
after having been, it again does not cease
to be; unborn, eternal, changeless, and
ancient, it is not killed when the body is
explanation:
As It is indivisible (Akhanda). It does
not diminish in size.

sanskrit:
वेदाविनाशिनं नित्यं य एनमजमव्ययम्।
कथं स पुरुषः पार्थ कं घातयति हन्ति कम्
translation:
Whoever knows it to be indestructible,
eternal, unborn, and inexhaustible, how
can that person slay, O Arjuna, or cause
to be slain?
explanation:
The enlightened sage who knows the
immutable and indestructible Self through
direct cognition or spiritual Anubhava
(experience) cannot do the act of slaying.

sanskrit:
वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहाय
नवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि।
तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णा
न्यन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही
translation:
Just as a man casts off worn-out clothes
and puts on new ones, so too the embodied
Self casts off worn-out bodies and enters
others that are new.
explanation:
As a man discards his threadbare robes and
puts on new ones, so the Spirit throws off
its worn-out bodies and takes on fresh
ones.

sanskrit:
नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः।
न चैनं क्लेदयन्त्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः
translation:
Weapons cannot cut it, fire cannot burn
it, water cannot wet it, wind cannot dry
it.
explanation: The Self is indivisible. It has no parts.

sanskrit:
अच्छेद्योऽयमदाह्योऽयमक्लेद्योऽशोष्य एव च।
नित्यः सर्वगतः स्थाणुरचलोऽयं सनातनः
translation:
This Self cannot be cut, burned, wetted,
nor dried up; it is eternal,
all-pervasive, stable, immovable, and
ancient.
explanation:
The Self is very subtle. It is beyond the
reach of speech and mind.

sanskrit:
अव्यक्तोऽयमचिन्त्योऽयमविकार्योऽयमुच्यते।
तस्मादेवं विदित्वैनं नानुशोचितुमर्हसि
translation:
This Self is said to be unmanifested,
unthinkable, and unchangeable. Therefore,
knowing this to be so, you should not
grieve.
explanation:
The Self is not an object of perception.
It can hardly be seen by the physical
eyes.

sanskrit:
अथ चैनं नित्यजातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम्।
तथापि त्वं महाबाहो नैवं शोचितुमर्हसि
translation:
But even if thou thinkest of It as
constantly being born and constantly
dying, even then, O mighty-armed one, thou
shouldst not grieve.
explanation:
Lord Krishna here? for the sake of
argument? takes up the popular
supposition. This is the inexorable or
unrelenting Law of Nature.

sanskrit:
जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च।
तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि
translation:
For the born, death is certain, and for
the dead, birth is certain; therefore, you
should not grieve over the inevitable.
explanation:
Birth is sure to happen to that which is
dead death is sure to happen to what which
is born. Birth and death are certainly
unavoidable.

sanskrit:
अव्यक्तादीनि भूतानि व्यक्तमध्यानि भारत।
अव्यक्तनिधनान्येव तत्र का परिदेवना
translation:
Beings are unmanifest in their beginning,
manifest in their middle state, O Arjuna,
and unmanifest again in their end. What is
there to grieve about?
explanation:
The physical body is a combination of the
five elements. It is seen by the physical
eyes only after the five elements have
entered into such combination.

sanskrit:
आश्चर्यवत्पश्यति कश्चिदेन
माश्चर्यवद्वदति तथैव चान्यः।
आश्चर्यवच्चैनमन्यः श्रृणोति
श्रुत्वाप्येनं वेद न चैव कश्चित्
translation:
One sees this (the Self) as a wonder;
another speaks of it as a wonder; another
hears of it as a wonder; yet, having
heard, none understands it at all.
explanation:
The verse may also be interpreted in this
manner. He that sees? hears and speaks of
the Self is a wonderful man.

sanskrit:
देही नित्यमवध्योऽयं देहे सर्वस्य भारत।
तस्मात्सर्वाणि भूतानि न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि
translation:
This indweller in the body of everyone is
ever indestructible, O Arjuna; therefore,
you should not grieve for any creature.
explanation:
The body of any creature may be destroyed
but the Self cannot be killed. Therefore
you should not grieve regarding any
creature whatever? Bhishma or anybody

sanskrit:
स्वधर्ममपि चावेक्ष्य न विकम्पितुमर्हसि।
धर्म्याद्धि युद्धाछ्रेयोऽन्यत्क्षत्रियस्य न विद्यते
translation:
Further, having regard to your duty, you
should not waver, for there is nothing
higher for a Kshatriya than a righteous
war.
explanation:
Lord Krishna now gives to Arjuna wordly
reasons for fighting. Up to this time? He
talked to Arjuna on the immortality of the
Self and gave him philosophical reasons.

sanskrit:
यदृच्छया चोपपन्नं स्वर्गद्वारमपावृतम्।
सुखिनः क्षत्रियाः पार्थ लभन्ते युद्धमीदृशम्
translation:
Happy are the Kshatriyas, O Arjuna! who
are called to fight in such a battle that
comes of its own accord as an open door to
heaven.
explanation:
The scriptures declare that if a Kshatriya
dies for a righteous cause on the
battlefield? he at once goes to heaven.

sanskrit:
अथ चैत्त्वमिमं धर्म्यं संग्रामं न करिष्यसि।
ततः स्वधर्मं कीर्तिं च हित्वा पापमवाप्स्यसि
translation:
But if you will not fight this righteous
war, then having abandoned your own duty
and reputation, you will incur sin.
explanation:
The Lord reminds Arjuna of the fame he had
already earned and which he would now lose
if he refused to fight. Arjuna had acired
great fame by fighting with Lord Siva.

sanskrit:
अकीर्तिं चापि भूतानि कथयिष्यन्ति तेऽव्ययाम्।
संभावितस्य चाकीर्तिर्मरणादतिरिच्यते
translation:
People will also recount your everlasting
dishonor; and for one who has been
honored, dishonor is worse than death.
explanation:
The world also will ever recount thy
infamy which will survive thee for a long
time. Death is really preferable to
disgrace to one who has been honoured as a

sanskrit:
भयाद्रणादुपरतं मंस्यन्ते त्वां महारथाः।
येषां च त्वं बहुमतो भूत्वा यास्यसि लाघवम्
translation:
The great chariot-warriors will think that
you have withdrawn from the battle out of
fear, and you will be held in low esteem
by those who have held you in high regard.
explanation:
Duryodhana and others will certainly think
that you have fled from the battle from
fear of Karna and others? but not through
compassion and reverence for elders and

sanskrit:
अवाच्यवादांश्च बहून् वदिष्यन्ति तवाहिताः।
निन्दन्तस्तव सामर्थ्यं ततो दुःखतरं नु किम्
translation:
Your enemies, scoffing at your power, will
speak many abusive words—what could be
more painful than this?
explanation:
There is really no pain more unbearable
and tormenting that that of slander thus
incurred.

sanskrit:
हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम्।
तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ कौन्तेय युद्धाय कृतनिश्चयः
translation:
Slain, you will obtain heaven; victorious,
you will enjoy the earth; therefore, stand
up, O son of Kunti, resolved to fight.
explanation:
In either case you will be benefited.
Therefore? stand up with the firm
resolution I will coner the enemy or die.

maintenance of the body would not be
possible for you through inaction.
explanation:
Niyatam Karma is an obligatory duty which
one is bound to perform. Thenonperformance
of the bounden duties causes demerit.

sanskrit:
यज्ञार्थात्कर्मणोऽन्यत्र लोकोऽयं कर्मबन्धनः।
तदर्थं कर्म कौन्तेय मुक्तसंगः समाचर
translation:
The world is bound by actions other than
those performed for the sake of sacrifice;
do thou, therefore, O son of Kunti
(Arjuna), perform actions for that sake
explanation:
Yajna means sacrifice or religious rite or
any unselfish action done with a pure
motive. It means also Isvara.

sanskrit:
सहयज्ञाः प्रजाः सृष्ट्वा पुरोवाच प्रजापतिः।
अनेन प्रसविष्यध्वमेष वोऽस्त्विष्टकामधुक्
translation:
The Creator, having in the beginning
created mankind together with sacrifice,
said, "By this shall you propagate; let
this be the milch cow of your desires—the
explanation:
Prajapati is the Creator or Brahma.
Kamadhuk is another name for the cow
Kamadhenu.

sanskrit:
देवान्भावयतानेन ते देवा भावयन्तु वः।
परस्परं भावयन्तः श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यथ
translation:
With this, nourish the gods, and may the
gods nourish you; thus, nourishing each
other, you shall attain the highest good.
explanation:
Deva literally means the shining one. By
this sacrifice you nourish the gods such
as Indra.

sanskrit:
इष्टान्भोगान्हि वो देवा दास्यन्ते यज्ञभाविताः।
तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो भुङ्क्ते स्तेन एव सः
translation:
The gods, nourished by the sacrifice, will
give you the desired objects. So, he who
enjoys the objects given by the gods
without offering anything in return is
explanation:
He who enjoys what has been given to him
by the gods? i.e.? he who gratifies the
cravings of his own body and the senses
without offering anything to the gods in

sanskrit:
यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तो मुच्यन्ते सर्वकिल्बिषैः।
भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात्
translation:
The righteous who eat the remnants of the
sacrifice are freed from all sins; but
those sinful ones who cook food solely for
their own sake indeed consume sin.
explanation:
These are the five places where injury to
life is daily committed. The sins are
washed away by the performance of the five
MahaYajnas or great sacrifices which every

sanskrit:
अन्नाद्भवन्ति भूतानि पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः।
यज्ञाद्भवति पर्जन्यो यज्ञः कर्मसमुद्भवः
translation:
From food come forth beings; from rain,
food is produced; from sacrifice arises
rain, and sacrifice is born of action.
explanation:
Here Yajna means Apurva or the subtle
principle or the unseen form which a
sacrifice assumes between the time of its
performance and the time when its fruits

sanskrit:
कर्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं विद्धि ब्रह्माक्षरसमुद्भवम्।
तस्मात्सर्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम्
translation:
Know that action comes from Brahma, and
Brahma comes from the Imperishable.
Therefore, the all-pervasive Brahma ever
rests in sacrifice.
explanation:
Brahma may mean Veda. Just as the breath
comes out of a man? so also the Veda is
the breath of the Imperishable or the
Omniscient.

sanskrit:
एवं प्रवर्तितं चक्रं नानुवर्तयतीह यः।
अघायुरिन्द्रियारामो मोघं पार्थ स जीवति
translation:
He who does not follow the wheel thus set
in motion, who is of sinful life,
rejoicing in the senses, lives in vain, O
Arjuna.
explanation:
This is the wheel of action set in motion
by the Creator on the basis of the Veda
and sacrifice.He who does not follow the
wheel by studying the Vedas and performing

sanskrit:
यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च मानवः।
आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते
translation:
But for that man who rejoices only in the
Self, who is satisfied with the Self and
is content in the Self alone, indeed there
is nothing to do.
explanation:
The sage does not depend on external
objects for his happiness. He is ite
satisfied with the Self.

sanskrit:
नैव तस्य कृतेनार्थो नाकृतेनेह कश्चन।
न चास्य सर्वभूतेषु कश्िचदर्थव्यपाश्रयः
translation:
For him, there is no interest whatsoever
in what is done or not done; nor does he
depend on any being for any purpose.
explanation:
The sage who is thus rejoicing in the Self
does not gain anything by doing any
action. For him really no purpose is
served by an action.

sanskrit:
तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर।
असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः
translation:
Therefore, without attachment, always
perform the actions that should be done;
for by performing actions without
attachment, one reaches the Supreme.
explanation:
If you perform actions without attachment?
for the sake of the Lord? you will attain
to Selfrealisation through purity of
heart. (Cf.II.64IV.19?23XVIII.49).

sanskrit:
कर्मणैव हि संसिद्धिमास्थिता जनकादयः।
लोकसंग्रहमेवापि संपश्यन्कर्तुमर्हसि
translation:
Janaka and others attained perfection
indeed through action alone; even with the
intention of protecting the masses, you
should perform action.
explanation:
Samsiddhi is Moksha (perfection or
liberation). Janaka? (Asvapati) and others
had perfect knowledge of the Self? and yet
they performed actions in order to set an

sanskrit:
यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः।
स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते
explanation:
Man is a social animal. He is an imitating
animal too.

sanskrit:
न मे पार्थास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किञ्चन।
नानवाप्तमवाप्तव्यं वर्त एव च कर्मणि
translation:
There is nothing in the three worlds, O
Arjuna, that needs to be done by Me, nor
is there anything unattained that needs to
be attained; yet I engage Myself in
explanation:
I am the Lord of the universe and
therefore I have no personal grounds to
engage. Myself in action.

sanskrit:
यदि ह्यहं न वर्तेयं जातु कर्मण्यतन्द्रितः।
मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः
translation:
For, should I not ever engage myself in
action, unwearied, people would in every
way follow my path, O Arjuna.
explanation:
If I remain inactive? people also will
imitate Me and keep iet. They will all
become Tamasic and pass into a state of
inertia.

sanskrit:
उत्सीदेयुरिमे लोका न कुर्यां कर्म चेदहम्।
सङ्करस्य च कर्ता स्यामुपहन्यामिमाः प्रजाः
translation:
These worlds would perish if I did not
perform action; I would be the author of
confusion of castes and destruction of
these beings.
explanation:
If I did not engage in action? people
would also be inactive. They would not do
their duties according to the Varnasrama
Dharma (code of morals governing their own

sanskrit:
सक्ताः कर्मण्यविद्वांसो यथा कुर्वन्ति भारत।
कुर्याद्विद्वांस्तथासक्तश्िचकीर्षुर्लोकसंग्रहम्
translation:
As the ignorant act out of attachment to
action, O Bharata, so should the wise act
without attachment, wishing for the
welfare of the world.
explanation:
The ignorant man works in expectation of
fruits. He says? I will do such and such
work and will get such and such fruit.

sanskrit:
न बुद्धिभेदं जनयेदज्ञानां कर्मसङ्गिनाम्।
जोषयेत्सर्वकर्माणि विद्वान् युक्तः समाचरन्
translation:
Let no wise man unsettle the minds of
ignorant people who are attached to
action; he should engage them in all
actions, himself fulfilling them with
explanation:
An ignorant may says to himelf? I shall do
this action and thery enjoy its fruit. A
wise man should not unsettle his belief.

sanskrit:
प्रकृतेः क्रियमाणानि गुणैः कर्माणि सर्वशः।
अहङ्कारविमूढात्मा कर्ताऽहमिति मन्यते
translation:
All actions are wrought in all cases by
the qualities of Nature alone. He whose
mind is deluded by egoism thinks, "I am
the doer."
explanation:
Prakriti or Pradhana or Nature is that
state in which the three Gunas? viz.?
Sattva? Rajas and Tamas exist in a state
of eilibrium. The man who is deluded by

sanskrit:
तत्त्ववित्तु महाबाहो गुणकर्मविभागयोः।
गुणा गुणेषु वर्तन्त इति मत्वा न सज्जते
translation:
But he who knows the Truth, O mighty-armed
Arjuna, about the divisions of the
qualities and their functions, knowing
that the Gunas, as senses, move amidst the
explanation:
He who knows the truth that the Self is
entirely distinct from the three Gunas and

actions. He who knows the truth about the

sanskrit:

तानकृत्स्नविदो मन्दान्कृत्स्नविन्न विचालयेत्
translation:
Those deluded by the qualities of Nature
are attached to the functions of the
qualities. The man of perfect knowledge
should not unsettle the foolish one who is
explanation:
The ignorant people do action with the
expectation of fruits. The wise people who
have the knowledge of the Self should not
distract the faith or conviction or belief

sanskrit:
मयि सर्वाणि कर्माणि संन्यस्याध्यात्मचेतसा।
निराशीर्निर्ममो भूत्वा युध्यस्व विगतज्वरः
translation:
Renouncing all actions in Me, with the
mind centered on the Self, free from hope
and egoism, and from mental fever, fight
thou.
explanation:
Surrender all the actions to Me with the
thought? I perform all actions for the
sake of the Lord.Fever means grief?
sorrow. (Cf.V.10XVIII.66).

sanskrit:
ये मे मतमिदं नित्यमनुतिष्ठन्ति मानवाः।
श्रद्धावन्तोऽनसूयन्तो मुच्यन्ते तेऽपि कर्मभिः
translation:
Those who constantly practice this
teaching of Mine with faith and without
caviling, they too are freed from actions.
explanation:
Sraddha is a mental attitude. It means
faith.

sanskrit:
ये त्वेतदभ्यसूयन्तो नानुतिष्ठन्ति मे मतम्।
सर्वज्ञानविमूढांस्तान्विद्धि नष्टानचेतसः
translation:
But those who criticize My teaching and do
not practice it, deprived of all knowledge
and lacking discernment, know them to be
doomed to destruction.
explanation:
The pigheaded people who are obstinate?
who find fault with the teachings of the
Lord and who do not practise them are
certainly doomed to destruction. They are

sanskrit:

प्रकृतिं यान्ति भूतानि निग्रहः किं करिष्यति
translation:
Even a wise man acts in accordance with
his own nature; beings will follow their
nature; what can restraint do?
explanation:
He who reads this verse will come to the
conclusion that there is no scope for mans
personal exertion. It is not so.

sanskrit:
इन्द्रियस्येन्द्रियस्यार्थे रागद्वेषौ व्यवस्थितौ।
तयोर्न वशमागच्छेत्तौ ह्यस्य परिपन्थिनौ
translation:
Attachment and aversion for the objects of
the senses abide in the senses; let no one
come under their sway; for, they are his
enemies.
explanation:
Each sense has got attraction for a
pleasant object and aversion for a
disagreeable object. If one can control
these two currents? viz.? attachment and

sanskrit:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्।
स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः
translation:
Better is one's own duty, though devoid of
merit, than the duty of another well
discharged. Better is death in one's own
duty; the duty of another is fraught with
explanation:
It is indeed better for man to die
discharging his own duty though destitute
of merit than for him to live doing the
duty of another though performed in a

sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच
अथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः।
अनिच्छन्नपि वार्ष्णेय बलादिव नियोजितः
translation:
Arjuna said, "But what compels man to
commit sin, even against his wishes, O
Varshneya (Krishna), as if constrained by
force?"
explanation:
Varshneya is one born in the family of the
Vrishnis? a name of Krishna.

sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच
काम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः।
महाशनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम्
translation:
The Blessed Lord said, "It is desire and
it is anger, both of the quality of Rajas,
all-devouring and all-sinful; know this as
the foe here in this world."
explanation:
He who possesses these six attributes and
who has a perfect knowledge of the origin
and the end of the universe is Bhagavan or
the Lord.The cause of all sin and wrong

sanskrit:
धूमेनाव्रियते वह्निर्यथाऽऽदर्शो मलेन च।
यथोल्बेनावृतो गर्भस्तथा तेनेदमावृतम्
translation:
As fire is enveloped by smoke, as a mirror
is covered by dust, and as an embryo is
surrounded by the amniotic sac, so is this
enveloped by that.
explanation:
This means the universe. This also means
knowledge.

sanskrit:
आवृतं ज्ञानमेतेन ज्ञानिनो नित्यवैरिणा।
कामरूपेण कौन्तेय दुष्पूरेणानलेन च
translation:
O Arjuna, wisdom is enveloped by this
constant enemy of the wise, in the form of
desire, which is insatiable like fire.
explanation:
Manu says? Desire can never be satiated or
cooled down by the enjoyment ofobjects.
But as fire blazes forth the more when fed
with Ghee (melted butter) and wood? so it

sanskrit:
इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिरस्याधिष्ठानमुच्यते।
एतैर्विमोहयत्येष ज्ञानमावृत्य देहिनम्
translation:
The senses, the mind, and the intellect
are said to be its seat; through these, it
deludes the embodied one, veiling their
wisdom.
explanation:
If the abode of the enemy is known it is
ite easy to kill him. So Lord Krishna like
a wise army general points out to Arjuna
the abode of desire so that he may be able

sanskrit:
तस्मात्त्वमिन्द्रियाण्यादौ नियम्य भरतर्षभ।
पाप्मानं प्रजहि ह्येनं ज्ञानविज्ञाननाशनम्
translation:
Therefore, O best of the Bharatas, control
your senses first and then kill this
sinful thing, which destroys knowledge and
realization.
explanation:
Jnana is knowledge obtained through the
study of scriptures. This is indirect
knowledge or Paroksha Jnana.

sanskrit:
इन्द्रियाणि पराण्याहुरिन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनः।
मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः
translation:
They say that the senses are superior to
the body; the mind is superior to the
senses; the intellect is superior to the
mind; and He (the Self) is superior even
explanation:
When compared with the physical body which
is gross? external and limited? the senses
are certainly superior as they are more
subtle? internal and have a wider range of

sanskrit:
एवं बुद्धेः परं बुद्ध्वा संस्तभ्यात्मानमात्मना।
जहि शत्रुं महाबाहो कामरूपं दुरासदम्
translation:
Thus, knowing Him who is superior to the
intellect and restraining the self by the
Self, slay thou, O mighty-armed Arjuna,
the enemy in the form of desire, hard to
explanation:
Restrain the lower self by the higher
Self. Subdue the lower mind by the higher
mind.

sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच
इमं विवस्वते योगं प्रोक्तवानहमव्ययम्।
विवस्वान् मनवे प्राह मनुरिक्ष्वाकवेऽब्रवीत्
translation:
The Blessed Lord said, "I taught this
imperishable Yoga to Vivasvan; he then
told it to Manu; Manu proclaimed it to
Ikshvaku.
explanation:
Vivasvan means the sun. Ikshvaku was the
son of Manu.

sanskrit:
एवं परम्पराप्राप्तमिमं राजर्षयो विदुः।
स कालेनेह महता योगो नष्टः परन्तप
translation:
This, handed down in regular succession by
the royal sages, was known. This Yoga,
however, has been lost here over time, O
Parantapa (burner of the foes).
explanation:
The royal sages Men who were kings and at
the same time sages also? learnt this
Yoga.Arjuna could burn or harass his foes?
like the sun? by the heat of his valour

sanskrit:
स एवायं मया तेऽद्य योगः प्रोक्तः पुरातनः।
भक्तोऽसि मे सखा चेति रहस्यं ह्येतदुत्तमम्
translation:
That same ancient yoga has been today
taught to you by me, for you are my
devotee and my friend; it is the supreme
secret.
explanation:
This Yoga contains profound and subtle
teachings. Hence it is the supreme secret
which is revealed by the Lord.

sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच
अपरं भवतो जन्म परं जन्म विवस्वतः।
कथमेतद्विजानीयां त्वमादौ प्रोक्तवानिति
translation:
Arjuna said, "Later was Thy birth, and
prior to it was the birth of Vivasvan (the
Sun); how am I to understand that Thou
hast taught this Yoga from the beginning?"
explanation:
Thy birth took place later in the hourse
of Vasudeva Vivasvan or Vivasvat (the Sun)
was born earlier in the beginning of
evolution. How am I to believe that Thou

sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच
बहूनि मे व्यतीतानि जन्मानि तव चार्जुन।
तान्यहं वेद सर्वाणि न त्वं वेत्थ परन्तप
translation:
The Blessed Lord said, "Many births of
Mine have passed, as well as of thine, O
Arjuna; I know them all, but thou knowest
not, O Parantapa (scorcher of foes)."
explanation:
You have no intuitional knowledge. The eye
of wisdom has not been opened in you on
account of your past actions.

sanskrit:
अजोऽपि सन्नव्ययात्मा भूतानामीश्वरोऽपि सन्।
प्रकृतिं स्वामधिष्ठाय संभवाम्यात्ममायया
translation:
Though I am unborn and of imperishable
nature, and though I am the Lord of all
beings, yet, governing my own nature, I am
born by my own Maya.
explanation: Man is bound by Karma. So he takes birth.

sanskrit:
यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत।
अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदाऽऽत्मानं सृजाम्यहम्
translation:
Whenever there is a decline of
righteousness and an increase of
unrighteousness, O Arjuna, then I manifest
Myself.
explanation:
Dharma is that which sustains and holds
together. There is no proper eivalen for
this term in the English language.

sanskrit:
परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम्।
धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय संभवामि युगे युगे
translation:
For the protection of the good, for the
destruction of the wicked, and for the
establishment of righteousness, I am born
in every age.
explanation:
To protect the righteous, to destroy the
wicked, and to establish the kingdom of
God, I am reborn from age to age.

sanskrit:
जन्म कर्म च मे दिव्यमेवं यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः।
त्यक्त्वा देहं पुनर्जन्म नैति मामेति सोऽर्जुन
translation:
He who thus knows, in their true light, My

पुरुषं शाश्वतं दिव्यमादिदेवमजं विभुम्
translation:
Arjuna said, "You are the Supreme Brahman,
the supreme abode, the supreme purifier,
eternal, divine Person, the primeval God,
unborn, and omnipresent."
explanation:
Param Brahma The highest Self. The word
Param indicates the pure and attributeless
Absolute? free from the limiting adjuncts.

sanskrit:
आहुस्त्वामृषयः सर्वे देवर्षिर्नारदस्तथा।
असितो देवलो व्यासः स्वयं चैव ब्रवीषि मे
translation:
All the sages have thus declared Thee, as
also the divine sage Narada; so also
Asita, Devala, and Vyasa; and now Thou
Thyself dost say so to me.
explanation:
Rishi is a holy sage of disciplined mind
and senses.Devarshi A divine sage more
highly evolved than a Rishi.

sanskrit:
सर्वमेतदृतं मन्ये यन्मां वदसि केशव।
न हि ते भगवन् व्यक्ितं विदुर्देवा न दानवाः
translation:
I believe all that You have said to me to
be true, O Krishna; indeed, O blessed
Lord! Neither the gods nor the demons know
Your manifestation (origin).
explanation:
As the Lord is the source of the gods? the
demons and others? they cannot comprehend
His manifestation or origin. (Cf.IV.6).

sanskrit:
स्वयमेवात्मनाऽत्मानं वेत्थ त्वं पुरुषोत्तम।
भूतभावन भूतेश देवदेव जगत्पते
translation:
Verily, Thou Thyself knowest Thyself by
Thyself, O Supreme Person, O source and
Lord of all beings, O God of gods, O ruler
of the world!
explanation:
Purushottama means the best among all
Purushas. Hence He is called
Purushottama.Devadeva is He who is
worshipped even by Indra and other

sanskrit:
वक्तुमर्हस्यशेषेण दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतयः।
याभिर्विभूतिभिर्लोकानिमांस्त्वं व्याप्य तिष्ठसि
translation:
You should indeed tell, without reserve,
of your divine glories by which you exist,
pervading all these worlds. (No one else
can do so.)
explanation:
Please tell me about all of Your glorious
manifestations, through which You pervade
the world.

sanskrit:
कथं विद्यामहं योगिंस्त्वां सदा परिचिन्तयन्।
केषु केषु च भावेषु चिन्त्योऽसि भगवन्मया
translation:
How shall I, ever meditating, know you, O
Yogin? In what aspects or things, O
blessed Lord, should I think of you?
explanation:
Arjuna says O Lord? how may I know Thee by
constant meditation In what aspects art
Thou to be thought of by me Even when I
think of external objects I can meditate

sanskrit:
विस्तरेणात्मनो योगं विभूतिं च जनार्दन।
भूयः कथय तृप्तिर्हि श्रृण्वतो नास्ति मेऽमृतम्
translation:
Tell me again in detail, O Krishna, of
your yogic power and glory; for I am not
satiated with what I have heard of your
life-giving and nectar-like speech.
explanation:
The Lord is called Janardana because all
pray to Him for worldly success?
prosperity and also salvation. Arjuna also
prays to the Lord to explain His Yogic

sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच
हन्त ते कथयिष्यामि दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतयः।
प्राधान्यतः कुरुश्रेष्ठ नास्त्यन्तो विस्तरस्य मे
translation:
The Blessed Lord said, "Very well! Now I
will declare to you My divine glories in
their prominence, O Arjuna; there is no
end to their detailed description."
explanation:
Now I will tell you of My most prominent
divine glories. My glories are illimitable
it is not possible to describe all of
them.

sanskrit:
अहमात्मा गुडाकेश सर्वभूताशयस्थितः।
अहमादिश्च मध्यं च भूतानामन्त एव च
translation:
I am the Self, O Gudakesa, seated in the
hearts of all beings; I am the beginning,
the middle, and the end of all beings.
explanation:
O Gudakesa I am the soul (Pratyagatma)
which exists in the hearts of all beings
and I am also the source or origin? the
middle or stay? and the end of all created

sanskrit:
आदित्यानामहं विष्णुर्ज्योतिषां रविरंशुमान्।
मरीचिर्मरुतामस्मि नक्षत्राणामहं शशी
translation:
Among the twelve Adityas, I am Vishnu;
among luminaries, the radiant sun; among
the seven or forty-nine Maruts, I am
Marichi; among stars, I am the moon.
explanation:
The twelve months of the year are the
Adityas.The Maruts are the gods
controlling the winds. You can practise
the same kind of meditation on all forms

sanskrit:
वेदानां सामवेदोऽस्मि देवानामस्मि वासवः।
इन्द्रियाणां मनश्चास्मि भूतानामस्मि चेतना
translation:
Among the Vedas, I am the Sama-Veda; among
the gods, I am Vasava; among the senses, I
am the mind; and among living beings, I am
intelligence.
explanation:
The mind is regarded as the eleventh
sense. As the senses cannot function
without the help of the mind? the mind is
regarded as the chief among the

sanskrit:
रुद्राणां शङ्करश्चास्मि वित्तेशो यक्षरक्षसाम्।
वसूनां पावकश्चास्मि मेरुः शिखरिणामहम्
translation:
And among the Rudras, I am Sankara; among
the Yakshas and Rakshasas, the Lord of
Wealth (Kubera); among the Vasus, I am
Pavaka (Fire); and among the seven
explanation:
Rudras are eleven in number. The ten vital
airs (Pranas and the UpaPranas? which are
five each) and the mind are the eleven
Rudras.

sanskrit:
पुरोधसां च मुख्यं मां विद्धि पार्थ बृहस्पतिम्।
सेनानीनामहं स्कन्दः सरसामस्मि सागरः
translation:
And, among the household priests of kings,
O Arjuna, know Me to be the chief,
Brihaspati; among the army generals, I am
Skanda; among lakes, I am the ocean.
explanation:
Brihaspati is the chif priest of the gods.
He is the househld priest of Indra.Skanda
is Kartikeya or Lord Subramanya.

sanskrit:
महर्षीणां भृगुरहं गिरामस्म्येकमक्षरम्।
यज्ञानां जपयज्ञोऽस्मि स्थावराणां हिमालयः
translation:
Among the great sages, I am Bhrigu; among
words, I am the one syllable (Om); among
sacrifices, I am the sacrifice of silent
repetition; among the immovable things, I
explanation:
Manu has said Whatever else the Brahmana
may or may not do? he attains salvation by
Japa (silent repetition of a Mantra)
alone.Bhrigu is one of the mindborn of the

sanskrit:
अश्वत्थः सर्ववृक्षाणां देवर्षीणां च नारदः।
गन्धर्वाणां चित्ररथः सिद्धानां कपिलो मुनिः
translation:
Among all the trees, I am the Peepul;
among the divine sages, I am Narada; among
the Gandharvas, I am Chitraratha; among
the perfected, I am the sage Kapila.
explanation:
Devarshis are gods and at the same time
Rishis or seers of Mantras.Siddhas are the
perfected ones those who at their very
birth attained without any effort Dharma

sanskrit:
उच्चैःश्रवसमश्वानां विद्धि माममृतोद्भवम्।
ऐरावतं गजेन्द्राणां नराणां च नराधिपम्
translation:
Know Me as Ucchaisravas, born of nectar,
among horses; Airavata among lordly
elephants; and the king among men.
explanation:
Nectar was obtained by the gods by
churning the ocean of milk. Ucchaisravas
is the name of the royal horse which was
born in that ocean of milk when it was

sanskrit:
आयुधानामहं वज्रं धेनूनामस्मि कामधुक्।
प्रजनश्चास्मि कन्दर्पः सर्पाणामस्मि वासुकिः
translation:
Among weapons, I am the thunderbolt; among
cows, I am the wish-fulfilling cow called
Kamadhenu; I am the progenitor, the god of
love; among serpents, I am Vasuki.
explanation:
Vajram the thunderbolt weapon made of the
bones of Dadhichi an implement of warfare
which can only be handled by Indra who has
fininshed a hundred sacrifices.Kamadhuk

sanskrit:
अनन्तश्चास्मि नागानां वरुणो यादसामहम्।
पितृ़णामर्यमा चास्मि यमः संयमतामहम्
translation:
I am Ananta among the Nagas; I am Varuna
among water-deities; Aryaman among the
Manes; I am Yama among the governors.
explanation:
Ananta is the king of hooded serpents or
cobras. He is firecoloured.Varuna is the
king of the watergods.Waterdeities The
gods connected with waters.Aryaman is the

sanskrit:
प्रह्लादश्चास्मि दैत्यानां कालः कलयतामहम्।
मृगाणां च मृगेन्द्रोऽहं वैनतेयश्च पक्षिणाम्
translation:
And I am Prahlada among the demons, I am
Time among reckoners, I am the lion among
beasts, and Vainateya (Garuda) among
birds.
explanation:
Prahlada? though he was the son of a demon
(Hiranyakasipu)? was a great devotee of
the Lord.

sanskrit:
पवनः पवतामस्मि रामः शस्त्रभृतामहम्।
झषाणां मकरश्चास्मि स्रोतसामस्मि जाह्नवी
translation:
Among the purifiers, I am the wind; among
the warriors, I am Rama; among the fishes,
I am the shark; among the streams, I am
the Ganga.
explanation:
The holy river Ganga (spelt Ganges in
English) was swallowed by Jahnu when she
was being brought down by Bhagiratha from
heaven. Hence the name Jahnavi for Ganga.

sanskrit:
सर्गाणामादिरन्तश्च मध्यं चैवाहमर्जुन।
अध्यात्मविद्या विद्यानां वादः प्रवदतामहम्
translation:
Among creations I am the beginning, the
middle, and the end, O Arjuna; among the
sciences, I am the science of the Self;
and I am the logic among
explanation:
I am the metaphysics among all sciences. I
am knowledge of the Self among all
branches of knowledge.

sanskrit:
अक्षराणामकारोऽस्मि द्वन्द्वः सामासिकस्य च।
अहमेवाक्षयः कालो धाताऽहं विश्वतोमुखः
translation:
Among the letters of the alphabet, I am
the letter 'A' and the dual among
compounds. I am verily the inexhaustible
and everlasting time; I am the dispenser
explanation: Among the alphabets I am the letter A.

sanskrit:
मृत्युः सर्वहरश्चाहमुद्भवश्च भविष्यताम्।
कीर्तिः श्रीर्वाक्च नारीणां स्मृतिर्मेधा धृतिः क्षमा
translation:
And I am the all-devouring Death, and the
source of prosperity for those who are to
be prosperous; among the feminine
qualities, I am fame, prosperity, speech,
explanation:
I am also the allsnatching death that
destroys everything. Death is of two
kinds? viz.? he who seizes wealth and he
who seizes life.

sanskrit:
बृहत्साम तथा साम्नां गायत्री छन्दसामहम्।
मासानां मार्गशीर्षोऽहमृतूनां कुसुमाकरः
translation:
Among the hymns, I am the Brihatsaman;
among meters, I am Gayatri; among months,
I am Margasirsha; among seasons, I am the
flowery season.
explanation:
Brihatsaman is the chief of the hymns of
the SamaVeda. Brihat means big.Margasirsha
From the middle of December to the middle
of January.

sanskrit:
द्यूतं छलयतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम्।
जयोऽस्मि व्यवसायोऽस्मि सत्त्वं सत्त्ववतामहम्
translation:
I am the gambling of the deceitful; I am
the splendor of the splendid; I am
victory; I am the resolve of the resolute;
I am the goodness of the good.
explanation:
Of the methods of defrauding others I am
gambling such as diceplay. Gambling is My
manifestation.

sanskrit:
वृष्णीनां वासुदेवोऽस्मि पाण्डवानां धनंजयः।
मुनीनामप्यहं व्यासः कवीनामुशना कविः
translation:
Among the Vrishnis, I am Vaasudeva; among
the Pandavas, I am Arjuna; among the
sages, I am Vyasa; among the poets, I am
Usanas, the poet.
explanation:
Vrishnis are Yadavas or the descendants of
Yadu. I am the foremost among them.Usanas
is Sukracharya? the preceptor of the
demons.

sanskrit:
दण्डो दमयतामस्मि नीतिरस्मि जिगीषताम्।
मौनं चैवास्मि गुह्यानां ज्ञानं ज्ञानवतामहम्
translation:
Of those who punish, I am the scepter;
among those who seek victory, I am
statesmanship; and among secrets, I am
silence; I am knowledge among knowers.
explanation:
Niti Diplomacy? polity.Maunam The silence
produced by constant meditation on Brahman
or the Self.Jnanam Knowledge of the Self.

sanskrit:
यच्चापि सर्वभूतानां बीजं तदहमर्जुन।
न तदस्ति विना यत्स्यान्मया भूतं चराचरम्
translation:
And whatever is the seed of all beings,
that too am I, O Arjuna; there is no
being, be it moving or unmoving, that can
exist without Me.
explanation:
I am the primeval seed from which all
creation has come into existence. I am the
seed of everything.

sanskrit:
नान्तोऽस्ति मम दिव्यानां विभूतीनां परंतप।
एष तूद्देशतः प्रोक्तो विभूतेर्विस्तरो मया
translation:
There is no end to My divine glories, O
Arjuna, but this is a brief statement by
Me of the particulars of My divine glory.
explanation:
It is impossible for anyone to describe or
know the exact extent of the divine
gloreis of the Lord. There is no limit to
His powers or glories.

sanskrit:
यद्यद्विभूतिमत्सत्त्वं श्रीमदूर्जितमेव वा।
तत्तदेवावगच्छ त्वं मम तेजोंऽशसंभवम्
translation:
Whatever being there is glorious,
prosperous, or powerful, know that to be a
manifestation of a part of My splendor.
explanation:
Whatever is glorious, excellent,
beautiful, and mighty, be assured that it
comes from a fragment of My splendor.

sanskrit:
अथवा बहुनैतेन किं ज्ञातेन तवार्जुन।
विष्टभ्याहमिदं कृत्स्नमेकांशेन स्थितो जगत्
translation:
But, of what avail is the knowledge of all
these details to you, O Arjuna? I exist,
supporting this whole world with one part
of Myself.
explanation:
The Lord concludes Having established or
pervaded this whole world with one
fragment of Myself? I remain.This verse is
based on the declaration in the Purusha

sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच
मदनुग्रहाय परमं गुह्यमध्यात्मसंज्ञितम्।
यत्त्वयोक्तं वचस्तेन मोहोऽयं विगतो मम
translation:
Arjuna said, By this explanation of the
highest secret concerning the Self which
Thou hast spoken, for the sake of blessing
me, my delusion has been dispelled.
explanation:
After hearing the glories of the Lord?
Arjuna has an intense longing to have the
wonderful vision of the Cosmic Form with
his own eyes. His bewilderment and

sanskrit:
भवाप्ययौ हि भूतानां श्रुतौ विस्तरशो मया।
त्वत्तः कमलपत्राक्ष माहात्म्यमपि चाव्ययम्
translation:
The origin and destruction of beings have
been heard in detail from You, O
lotus-eyed Lord, and also Your
inexhaustible greatness.
explanation:
Kamalapatraksha Lotuseyed or having eyes
like lotuspetals. Kamalapatra also means
knowledge of the Self.

sanskrit:
एवमेतद्यथात्थ त्वमात्मानं परमेश्वर।
द्रष्टुमिच्छामि ते रूपमैश्वरं पुरुषोत्तम
translation:
Now, O Supreme Lord, as Thou hast thus
described Thyself, O Supreme Person, I
wish to behold Thy divine form.
explanation:
Some commentators take the two halves of
this verse as two independent sentences
and interpret it thusSo it is? O Supreme
Lord? as Thou hast declared Thyself to be.

sanskrit:
मन्यसे यदि तच्छक्यं मया द्रष्टुमिति प्रभो।
योगेश्वर ततो मे त्वं दर्शयाऽत्मानमव्ययम्
translation:
If Thou, O Lord, thinkest it possible for
me to see it, do Thou, then, O Lord of the
Yogis, show me Thy imperishable Self.
explanation:
Arjuna is very keen and eager to see the
Cosmic Form of the Lord. He prays to Him
to grant him the vision.

sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच
पश्य मे पार्थ रूपाणि शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः।
नानाविधानि दिव्यानि नानावर्णाकृतीनि च
translation:
The Blessed Lord said, "Behold, O Arjuna,
forms of Mine, by the hundreds and
thousands, of different sorts, divine, and
of various colors and shapes."
explanation:
Divyani Divine supernatural.Satasah?
Sahasrasah By the hundreds and thousands
-- countless.O Arjuna? I want you to
behold the Cosmic Form. All beings and

sanskrit:
पश्यादित्यान्वसून्रुद्रानश्िवनौ मरुतस्तथा।
बहून्यदृष्टपूर्वाणि पश्याऽश्चर्याणि भारत
translation:
Behold the Adityas, the Vasus, the Rudras,
the two Asvins, and the Maruts; behold
many wonders never before seen, O Arjuna.
explanation:
Adityas? Vasus? Rudras and Maruts have
already been described in the previous
chapter.Not these alone Behold also many
other wonders never seen before by you or

sanskrit:
इहैकस्थं जगत्कृत्स्नं पश्याद्य सचराचरम्।
मम देहे गुडाकेश यच्चान्यद्द्रष्टुमिच्छसि
translation:
Now, behold, O Arjuna, in this My body,
the entire universe centered in one,
including the moving and the unmoving, and
whatever else you desire to see.
explanation:
Anyat Other whatever else. Your success or
defeat in the war? about which you,have
entertained a doubt.

sanskrit:
न तु मां शक्यसे द्रष्टुमनेनैव स्वचक्षुषा।
दिव्यं ददामि ते चक्षुः पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम्
translation:
But you are not able to behold Me with
these your own eyes; I give you the divine
eye; behold My lordly Yoga.
explanation:
No fleshly eyes can behold Me in My Cosmic
Form. One can see It through the divine
eye or the eye of intuition.

sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच
एवमुक्त्वा ततो राजन्महायोगेश्वरो हरिः।
दर्शयामास पार्थाय परमं रूपमैश्वरम्
translation:
Sanjaya said, Having thus spoken, O king,
the great Lord of Yoga, Hari (Krishna),
showed Arjuna His supreme form as the
Lord.
explanation:
King This verse is addressed by Sanjaya to
Dhritarashtra.Supreme Form The Cosmic
Form.

sanskrit:
अनेकवक्त्रनयनमनेकाद्भुतदर्शनम्।
अनेकदिव्याभरणं दिव्यानेकोद्यतायुधम्
translation:
With numerous mouths and eyes, with
numerous wondrous sights, with numerous
divine adornments, with numerous divine
weapons uplifted, such a form He showed.
explanation:
Countless faces appeared there. Arjuna
looked at this Cosmic Form in all its
magnificence.

sanskrit:
दिव्यमाल्याम्बरधरं दिव्यगन्धानुलेपनम्।
सर्वाश्चर्यमयं देवमनन्तं विश्वतोमुखम्
translation:
Wearing divine garlands and apparel,
anointed with divine unguents, the
all-wonderful, resplendent Being is
endless with faces on all sides.
explanation:
Visvatomukham With faces on all sides? as
He is the Self of all beings.Devam God.
Also means resplendent.Anantam Endless.
