world. He fills and surrounds this world
with Himself.

sanskrit: सर्वेन्द्रियगुणाभासं सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जितम्।असक्तं सर्वभृच्चैव निर्गुणं गुणभोक्तृ च
translation:
Shining by the functions of all the
senses, yet without being attached to
them; unattached, yet supporting all;
devoid of qualities, yet the experiencer
explanation:
He is the unseen seer? the unheard hearer?
the unthought thinker. Other than Him
there is no seer? no hearer? no thinker.

sanskrit: बहिरन्तश्च भूतानामचरं चरमेव च।सूक्ष्मत्वात्तदविज्ञेयं दूरस्थं चान्तिके च तत्
translation:
It is within and without all beings, both
the unmoving and the moving; It is subtle
and unknowable, and It is near and far
away.
explanation:
Brahman is subtle like the ether. It is
incomprehensible to the unillumined on
account of Its extreme subtlety.

sanskrit: अविभक्तं च भूतेषु विभक्तमिव च स्थितम्।भूतभर्तृ च तज्ज्ञेयं ग्रसिष्णु प्रभविष्णु च
translation:
Undivided yet, It exists as if divided in
beings; It is to be known as the supporter
of beings; It devours and It generates.
explanation:
It is undivided in the various bodies. It
is like ether.

sanskrit: ज्योतिषामपि तज्ज्योतिस्तमसः परमुच्यते।ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं ज्ञानगम्यं हृदि सर्वस्य विष्ठितम्
translation:
That Light of all lights is said to be
beyond darkness: knowledge, the knowable,
and the goal of knowledge, seated in the
hearts of all.
explanation:
It is selfluminous? The sun does not shine
there? nor do the moon and the stars? nor
do these lightnings shine and much less
this fire. When It shines? everything

sanskrit: इति क्षेत्रं तथा ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं चोक्तं समासतः।मद्भक्त एतद्विज्ञाय मद्भावायोपपद्यते
translation:
Thus, the field, as well as knowledge and
the knowable, have been briefly stated. My
devotee, knowing this, enters into My
being.
explanation:
Thus, I have briefly told you what Matter
is, the Self worth realizing, and what
Wisdom is. He who is devoted to Me knows,
and he will assuredly enter into Me.

sanskrit: प्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव विद्ध्यनादी उभावपि।विकारांश्च गुणांश्चैव विद्धि प्रकृतिसंभवान्
translation:
Know that Nature (matter) and the Spirit
are both beginningless, and know also that
all modifications and qualities are born
from Nature.
explanation:
Steps are necessary to reach the top floor
of a building. Even so? steps are
necessary to reach the summit of the
knowledge of the Self.

sanskrit: कार्यकारणकर्तृत्वे हेतुः प्रकृतिरुच्यते।पुरुषः सुखदुःखानां भोक्तृत्वे हेतुरुच्यते
translation:
In the production of the effect and the
cause, Nature (matter) is said to be the
cause; in the experience of pleasure and
pain, the soul is said to be the one
explanation:
Pleasure and pain are the fruits of
virtuous and vicious actions. The force of
desire acts on the mind and the mind
impels the senses to act to get the

sanskrit: पुरुषः प्रकृतिस्थो हि भुङ्क्ते प्रकृतिजान्गुणान्।कारणं गुणसङ्गोऽस्य सदसद्योनिजन्मसु
translation:
The soul seated in Nature experiences the
qualities born of Nature; attachment to
the qualities is the cause of its birth in
good and evil wombs.
explanation:
The soul residing in Nature and
identifying itself with the body and the
senses which are modifications of Nature
acts through the alities of Nature and

sanskrit: उपद्रष्टाऽनुमन्ता च भर्ता भोक्ता महेश्वरः।परमात्मेति चाप्युक्तो देहेऽस्मिन्पुरुषः परः
translation:
The Supreme Soul in this body is also
called the observer, the permitter, the
sustainer, the enjoyer, the great Lord,
and the Supreme Self.
explanation:
When the priests and the sacrificer
perform the sacrificial rites? an expert
who has good experience in sacrifical
matters sits by their side. He does not

sanskrit: य एवं वेत्ति पुरुषं प्रकृतिं च गुणैःसह।सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि न स भूयोऽभिजायते
translation:
He who thus knows the Spirit and Matter
together with their qualities, in whatever
condition he may be, he is not reborn.
explanation:
One who knows the Soul and Nature with its
alities? whatever his conduct may be?
frees himself from the cycle of births and
deaths. Such is the advantage he gains

sanskrit: ध्यानेनात्मनि पश्यन्ति केचिदात्मानमात्मना।अन्ये सांख्येन योगेन कर्मयोगेन चापरे
translation:
Some behold the Self within themselves
through meditation, others through the
Yoga of knowledge, and still others
through the Yoga of action.
explanation:
There are severla paths to reach the
knowledge of the Self according to the
nature or temperament and capacity of the
individual. The first path is the Yoga of

sanskrit: अन्ये त्वेवमजानन्तः श्रुत्वाऽन्येभ्य उपासते।तेऽपि चातितरन्त्येव मृत्युं श्रुतिपरायणाः
translation:
Others, too, who do not know thus,
worship, having heard of It from others;
they, too, cross beyond death, regarding
what they have heard as the supreme
explanation:
In this verse the Yoga of worship is
described.Some who are ignorant of the
methods described in the previous verse
listen to the teachings of the spiritual

sanskrit: यावत्सञ्जायते किञ्चित्सत्त्वं स्थावरजङ्गमम्।क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञसंयोगात्तद्विद्धि भरतर्षभ
translation:
Wherever a being is born, whether unmoving
or moving, know thou, O best of the
Bharatas (Arjuna), that it is from the
union of the field and its knower.
explanation:
O Arjuna? remember that whatever is born?
unmoving or moving? know thou that to be
done to the union between the body and the
Self.The knower of the field is like the

sanskrit: समं सर्वेषु भूतेषु तिष्ठन्तं परमेश्वरम्।विनश्यत्स्वविनश्यन्तं यः पश्यति स पश्यति
translation:
He who sees the Supreme Lord existing
truly in all beings, the imperishable
within the perishable, sees indeed.
explanation:
He who beholds the Supreme Lord through
the inner eye of wisdom? Him Who is seated
in all beings from the Creator down to the
unmoving objects and Who is not destroyed

sanskrit: समं पश्यन्हि सर्वत्र समवस्थितमीश्वरम्।न हिनस्त्यात्मनाऽऽत्मानं ततो याति परां गतिम्
translation:
For he who truly sees the same Lord
dwelling everywhere does not destroy the
Self by the self; rather, he attains the
highest goal.
explanation:
This is the vision of a liberated sage.
The Supreme Self abides in all forms.

sanskrit: प्रकृत्यैव च कर्माणि क्रियमाणानि सर्वशः।यः पश्यति तथाऽऽत्मानमकर्तारं स पश्यति
translation:
He sees, who sees that all actions are
performed solely by Nature and that the
Self is without action.
explanation:
Nature is responsible for all activities.
The Self is beyond all action.

sanskrit: यदा भूतपृथग्भावमेकस्थमनुपश्यति।तत एव च विस्तारं ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा
translation:
When a person sees all beings as resting
in the One and emanating from the One
alone, they then become Brahman.
explanation:
He who sees the diverse forms of life all
rooted in One and growing forth from Him,
shall indeed find the Absolute.

sanskrit: अनादित्वान्निर्गुणत्वात्परमात्मायमव्ययः।शरीरस्थोऽपि कौन्तेय न करोति न लिप्यते
translation:
Being without beginning, devoid of any
qualities, the Supreme Self, imperishable,
though dwelling in the body, O Arjuna,
neither acts nor is tainted.
explanation:
The Supreme Self is beyond Nature.
Therefore It is without alities.

sanskrit: यथा सर्वगतं सौक्ष्म्यादाकाशं नोपलिप्यते।सर्वत्रावस्थितो देहे तथाऽऽत्मा नोपलिप्यते
translation:
As the all-pervading ether is not tainted,
due to its subtlety, so the Self seated
everywhere in the body is not tainted
either.
explanation:
Ether pervades everything. All are
immersed in it.

sanskrit: यथा प्रकाशयत्येकः कृत्स्नं लोकमिमं रविः।क्षेत्रं क्षेत्री तथा कृत्स्नं प्रकाशयति भारत
translation:
Just as the one sun illuminates the entire
world, so too does the Lord of the field
(Supreme Self) illuminate the entire
field, O Arjuna.
explanation:
The Supreme Self is one. It illumines the
whole matter from the Unmanifested down to
the blade of grass or a lump of clay? from
the great elements down to firmness or

sanskrit: क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोरेवमन्तरं ज्ञानचक्षुषा।भूतप्रकृतिमोक्षं च ये विदुर्यान्ति ते परम्
translation:
They who, by the eye of knowledge,
perceive the distinction between the field
and its knower, as well as the liberation
from the Nature of being, go to the
explanation:
Through the attainment of Selfrealisation
or knowledge of the Self? they are
entirely liberated from the clutches or
the influence of Maya (delusion) and

sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचपरं भूयः प्रवक्ष्यामि ज्ञानानां ज्ञानमुत्तमम्।यज्ज्ञात्वा मुनयः सर्वे परां सिद्धिमितो गताः
translation:
The Blessed Lord said, "I will again
declare to thee that supreme knowledge,
the best of all knowledge, having known
which all the sages have gone to supreme
explanation:
Further analysis of the field is made in
this chapter.In chapter XIII? verse 21? it
has been stated that attachment to the
alities is the cause of Samsara or births

sanskrit: इदं ज्ञानमुपाश्रित्य मम साधर्म्यमागताः।सर्गेऽपि नोपजायन्ते प्रलये न व्यथन्ति च
translation:
Those who, having taken refuge in this
knowledge, have attained unity with Me,
are neither born at the time of creation
nor disturbed at the time of dissolution.
explanation:
Having resorted to this knowledge they
(the sages) are assimilated into My own
nature. They have attained to My Being.

sanskrit: मम योनिर्महद्ब्रह्म तस्मिन् गर्भं दधाम्यहम्।संभवः सर्वभूतानां ततो भवति भारत
translation:
My womb is the great Brahma; in it I place
the germ; thence, O Arjuna, is the birth
of all beings.
explanation:
My womb is the great Nature. The cosmos is
evolved out of His Nature.

sanskrit: सर्वयोनिषु कौन्तेय मूर्तयः सम्भवन्ति याः।तासां ब्रह्म महद्योनिरहं बीजप्रदः पिता
translation:
Whatever forms are produced, O Arjuna, in
any womb whatsoever, the great Brahma is
their womb, and I am the seed-giving
father.
explanation:
I am the father The Primordial Nature is
the mother. The whole manifested world is
the child Nature has produced in its
association with me.

sanskrit: सत्त्वं रजस्तम इति गुणाः प्रकृतिसंभवाः।निबध्नन्ति महाबाहो देहे देहिनमव्ययम्
translation:
These qualities, O Arjuna, born of Nature,
bind fast in the body of the embodied, the
indestructible: purity, passion, and
inertia.
explanation: Sattva is the best. Rajas comes next.

sanskrit: तत्र सत्त्वं निर्मलत्वात्प्रकाशकमनामयम्।सुखसङ्गेन बध्नाति ज्ञानसङ्गेन चानघ
translation:
Of these, sattva, which is luminous and
healthy due to its stainlessness, binds
one by attachment to happiness and
knowledge, O sinless one.
explanation:
Sattva is stainless like the crystal. It
lays for one the trap of happiness and
knowledge.

sanskrit: रजो रागात्मकं विद्धि तृष्णासङ्गसमुद्भवम्।तन्निबध्नाति कौन्तेय कर्मसङ्गेन देहिनम्
translation:
Know, O Arjuna, that Rajas is of the
nature of passion, the source of thirst
and attachment; it binds fast the embodied
one by attachment to action.
explanation:
The ality of Rajas denotes activity and
ambition. The Rajasic man is full of
cravings and desires.

sanskrit: तमस्त्वज्ञानजं विद्धि मोहनं सर्वदेहिनाम्।प्रमादालस्यनिद्राभिस्तन्निबध्नाति भारत
translation:
But know thou Tamas to be born of
ignorance, deluding all embodied beings;
it binds fast, O Arjuna, through
heedlessness, indolence, and sleep.
explanation:
Tamas is that binding force with a
tendency to lethargy? sloth and foolish
actions. It causes delusion or
nondiscrimination.

sanskrit: सत्त्वं सुखे सञ्जयति रजः कर्मणि भारत।ज्ञानमावृत्य तु तमः प्रमादे सञ्जयत्युत
translation:
Sattva attaches to happiness, Rajas to
action, O Arjuna, while Tamas, verily
shrouding knowledge, attaches to
heedlessness.
explanation:
Just as a dark cloud enshrouds the sun? so
also Tamas envelops knowledge or the light
of the Self. Tamas creates an attachment
for heedlessness? that is? ignorance or

sanskrit: रजस्तमश्चाभिभूय सत्त्वं भवति भारत।रजः सत्त्वं तमश्चैव तमः सत्त्वं रजस्तथा
translation:
Now, O Arjuna, Sattva prevails, having
overpowered Rajas and Tamas; then Rajas,
having overpowered Sattva and Tamas; and
then Tamas, having overpowered Sattva and
explanation:
Just as winter has its sway when summer
and autumn have gone? just as sleep has
its sway when a man is neither dreaming
nor waking? so also Sattva has its sway

sanskrit: सर्वद्वारेषु देहेऽस्मिन्प्रकाश उपजायते।ज्ञानं यदा तदा विद्याद्विवृद्धं सत्त्वमित्युत
translation:
When the wisdom-light shines through every
gate of this body, then it may be known
that Sattva is predominant.
explanation:
When a particular ality becomes
predominant? it reveals its distinctive
characteristics in man. Just as jasmine
scatters its fragrance far and wide? so

sanskrit: लोभः प्रवृत्तिरारम्भः कर्मणामशमः स्पृहा।रजस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे भरतर्षभ
translation:
Greed, activity, the undertaking of
actions, restlessness, and longing—these
arise when Rajas is predominant, O Arjuna.
explanation:
Greed Covetousness Desire to appropriate
the property of others a desire to possess
more wealth though one has sufficient
already.Pravritti Action in general.Asamah

sanskrit: अप्रकाशोऽप्रवृत्तिश्च प्रमादो मोह एव च।तमस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे कुरुनन्दन
translation:
Darkness, inertia, carelessness, and
delusion—these arise when Tamas is
predominant, O Arjuna.
explanation:
When Tamas increases? darkness? a desire
to do nothing? forgetfulness of ones
duties and confusion ome into
existence.Darkness Absence of

sanskrit: यदा सत्त्वे प्रवृद्धे तु प्रलयं याति देहभृत्।तदोत्तमविदां लोकानमलान्प्रतिपद्यते
translation:
If the embodied one meets death when
Sattva is predominant, then they attain
the spotless worlds of the knowers of the
Highest.
explanation:
Lokan Amalan Sptless worlds Brahmaloka and
the like where Rajas and Tamas never
predominate.The Highest Deities such as
Hiranyagarbha.

sanskrit: रजसि प्रलयं गत्वा कर्मसङ्गिषु जायते।तथा प्रलीनस्तमसि मूढयोनिषु जायते
translation:
Meeting death in Rajas, he is born among
those who are attached to action; and
dying in Tamas, he is born in the womb of
the thoughtless.
explanation:
Meeting with death in Rajas If he dies
when Rajas is predominant in him? he is
born among men who are attached to action.
If he dies when Tamas is fully predominant

sanskrit: कर्मणः सुकृतस्याहुः सात्त्विकं निर्मलं फलम्।रजसस्तु फलं दुःखमज्ञानं तमसः फलम्
translation:
They say that the fruit of good action is
Sattvic and pure; indeed, the fruit of
Rajas is pain, and the fruit of Tamas is
ignorance.
explanation:
Good action Sattvic action. The fruit of
good action is both happiness
and,knowledge.They The wise.Rajas means
Rajasic action as this verse deals with

sanskrit: सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च।प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतोऽज्ञानमेव च
translation:
From Sattva arises knowledge, and greed
from Rajas; heedlessness and delusion
arise from Tamas, and also ignorance.
explanation:
From Sattva When Sattva becomes
predominant. Sattva awakesn knowledge just
as the sun causes daylight.

sanskrit: ऊर्ध्वं गच्छन्ति सत्त्वस्था मध्ये तिष्ठन्ति राजसाः।जघन्यगुणवृत्तिस्था अधो गच्छन्ति तामसाः
translation:
Those seated in Sattva ascend; those of
Rajasic nature dwell in the middle; and
those of Tamasic nature, abiding in the
function of the lowest Guna, descend.
explanation:
Those who abide in Sattva become the lords
of heaven after giving up the physical
body. The Rajasic are rorn on this earth
as human beings.

sanskrit: नान्यं गुणेभ्यः कर्तारं यदा द्रष्टानुपश्यति।गुणेभ्यश्च परं वेत्ति मद्भावं सोऽधिगच्छति
translation:
When the seer beholds no agent other than
the Gunas and knows that which is higher
than them, he attains to My Being.
explanation:
The Supreme Self is in no way contaminated
by the alities. The liberated sage
exclaims I am the witness of the alities.

sanskrit: गुणानेतानतीत्य त्रीन्देही देहसमुद्भवान्।जन्ममृत्युजरादुःखैर्विमुक्तोऽमृतमश्नुते
translation:
The embodied one, having crossed beyond
these three Gunas from which the body is
evolved, is freed from birth, death,
decay, and pain, and attains immortality.
explanation:
He ever enjoys the bliss of the Eternal.
He attains release or Moksha.

sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचकैर्लिंगैस्त्रीन्गुणानेतानतीतो भवति प्रभो।किमाचारः कथं चैतांस्त्रीन्गुणानतिवर्तते
translation:
Arjuna said, "What are the marks of one
who has transcended the three qualities, O
Lord? What is their conduct, and how do
they go beyond these three qualities?"
explanation:
Arjuna said O Lord? by what
characteristics may a man be recognised as
having gone beyond the three alities What
is the behaviour of that Trigunatita sage

sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचप्रकाशं च प्रवृत्तिं च मोहमेव च पाण्डव।न द्वेष्टि सम्प्रवृत्तानि न निवृत्तानि काङ्क्षति
translation:
The Blessed Lord said, "When light,
activity, and delusion are present, he
does not hate them, nor does he long for
them when they are absent.
explanation:
This is the answer to Arjunas first
estion. Light is the effect of Sattva?
activity of Rajas and delusion of Tamas.

sanskrit: उदासीनवदासीनो गुणैर्यो न विचाल्यते।गुणा वर्तन्त इत्येव योऽवतिष्ठति नेङ्गते
translation:
He who, seated like one unconcerned, is
not moved by the dualities, and who,
knowing that the dualities are active, is
self-centered and does not move.
explanation:
He is seated as a neutral (one who
inclines to neither party). He is free
from likes and dislikes.

sanskrit: समदुःखसुखः स्वस्थः समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः।तुल्यप्रियाप्रियो धीरस्तुल्यनिन्दात्मसंस्तुतिः
translation:
Who is the same in pleasure and pain, who
dwells in the Self, to whom a clod of
earth, a stone, and gold are all alike,
who is the same to the dear and the
explanation:
Night and day have no meaning to a post

He is the perception of the ear, the eye,

Becoming the fire of life, I pass into

sanskrit: भक्त्या मामभिजानाति यावान्यश्चास्मि तत्त्वतः।ततो मां तत्त्वतो ज्ञात्वा विशते तदनन्तरम्
translation:
By devotion, he knows Me in truth, who and
what I am; then, having known Me in truth,
he immediately enters into the Supreme.
explanation:
My devotee? O Arjuna? who has attained to
union with Me through singleminded and
unflinching devotion is verily My very
Self. Devotion culminates in knowledge.

sanskrit: सर्वकर्माण्यपि सदा कुर्वाणो मद्व्यपाश्रयः।मत्प्रसादादवाप्नोति शाश्वतं पदमव्ययम्
translation:
Having taken refuge in Me and doing all
actions, by My grace he obtains the
eternal, indestructible state of being.
explanation:
Worshipping Me with the flowers of his
good actions he reaches the imperishable
Brahmic seat of ineffable splendour
through My grace. He attains union with Me

translation:
Mentally renouncing all actions in Me,
having Me as the highest goal, and
resorting to the yoga of discrimination,
do thou ever fix thy mind on Me.
explanation:

actions to Me whilst at the same time
fixing thy mind on discrimination. Then

Fixing your mind on Me, you shall, by My
grace, overcome all obstacles; but if you

translation:
O Arjuna, bound by your own Karma (action)
born of your own nature, that which from
delusion you wish not to do, even that you
shall do helplessly.
explanation:
Thou art? therefore? bound by these innate
alities. Thou wilt be forced to fight by
thy own nature.

sanskrit: ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशेऽर्जुन तिष्ठति।भ्रामयन्सर्वभूतानि यन्त्रारूढानि मायया
translation:
The Lord dwells in the hearts of all
beings, O Arjuna, causing all beings, by
His illusory power, to revolve as if
mounted on a machine.
explanation:
Isvara The Lord the Ruler of the universe
Narayana.The Lord abides in the hearts of
all beings. It is He Who has given a gift
of this marvellous machine to you.

sanskrit: तमेव शरणं गच्छ सर्वभावेन भारत।तत्प्रसादात्परां शान्तिं स्थानं प्राप्स्यसि शाश्वतम्
translation:
Fly to Him for refuge with all your being,
O Arjuna; by His grace you will obtain
supreme peace and the eternal abode.
explanation:
Do total and perfect surrender to the
Lord. Do not keep any secret desires for
silent gratification.

sanskrit: इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं मया।विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु
translation:
Thus, wisdom more secret than secrecy
itself has been declared to you by me.
Reflect on it fully, then act as you wish.
explanation:
Thus has wisdom? more profound than all
secrets? been declared to thee by Me. This
teaching is well known as the Gita? the
essence of all the Vedas.

sanskrit: सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः श्रृणु मे परमं वचः।इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम्
translation:
Hear again My supreme word, most secret of
all; for you are dearly beloved of Me, I
will tell you what is good.
explanation:
Now listen once more with rapt attention
to My words. Thou art very dear to Me.

translation:
Fix your mind on Me, be devoted to Me,
sacrifice to Me, bow down to Me. You will
come to Me; I truly promise you this, for
you are dear to Me.
explanation:
Develop onepointedness of mind. Fix thy
thought on Me.

translation:
Never speak this to one who is devoid of
austerities or devotion, who does not
render service, who does not desire to
listen, or who cavils at Me.
explanation:
Do not speak this to one who has not
practiced austerities, or to one who does
not love, or who will not listen, or who
mocks.

translation:
There is no one among men who does service
dearer to Me, nor shall there be anyone on
earth dearer to Me than him.
explanation:
He who hands down this Gita to My devotees
does immense service to Me. He is very
dear to Me.

translation:
And he who studies this sacred dialogue of
ours, by him I shall have been worshipped
through the sacrifice of wisdom; such is
my conviction.
explanation:
There are four kinds of sacrifice --
Vidhi? Japa? Upamsu and Manasa. Vidhi is
ritual.

Also, the man who hears this, full of
faith and free from malice, shall attain

Liberated from sin.Punyakarmanam Of those

Has this been heard, O Arjuna, with
one-pointed focus? Has the delusion of
your ignorance been destroyed, O
Dhananjaya?

It is the duty of the spiritual teacher or
preceptor to make the aspirant understand
the teaching of the scripture and to
enable him to attain the goal of life
